rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING PROVISIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT 10667, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS 'AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A NATIONAL COMPETITION POLICY PROHIBITING ANTI-COMPETITIVE AGREEMENTS, ABUSE OF DOMINANT POSITION AND ANTI-COMPETITIVE MERGERS AND ACQUISITIONS, ESTABLISHING THE PHILIPPINE COMPETITION COMMISSION AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR'
rows.abstract:
Seeks to amend the Philippine Competition Act to enhance the PCC's ability to enforce its mandate, particularly in investigating cartels, bid rigging, market foreclosure, and other anti-competitive conduct, as well as imposing various fines, penalties, and remedies.

Intends to legislate principles of the National Competition Policy to ensure the competition considerations are included in the formulation and deliberation of government policies; and mandates PCC to review fiscal incentives for anti-competitive effects.

Intends to make available affordable decent housing and basic services to underprivileged and homeless citizens in urban centers and resettlement areas.

rows.author: C102
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A BASIC REGULATORY FRAMEWORK FOR VIRTUAL BANKING AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Defines virtual bank as “a bank which primarily delivers retail banking services through the internet or other forms of electronic channels instead of physical branches”.

Seeks to regulate the existence of a financial system that is accessible to as wide a proportion of the population as possible which is a prerequisite to building a strong middle class; present opportunities for fast, reliable, and less costly delivery of social cash transfers; and expedite the rollout of critical anti-poverty measures and help achieve the country's inclusive growth goals.

Promotes the development of financial technology; grants adequate latitude to the BSP; auctions license to qualified virtual banking applicants; provides operations and management rules that levels the playing field; opens the sector to some degree of foreign ownership; outlines a framework for consumer protection including deposit insurance and protection against unauthorized transactions.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BANKS AND FINANCIAL INTERMEDIARIES since 2020-01-20

rows.author: J089
rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING HIGHER EDUCATION INSTITUTIONS AND TECHNICAL-VOCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS TO ENSURE THE SAFETY AND SECURITY OF THE ACADEMIC COMMUNITY FROM INTERNAL AND EXTERNAL THREATS, THEREBY CREATING A SAFETY AND SECURITY COMMITTEE FOR THIS PURPOSE AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Tasks HEIs and TVIs to provide for: a) a safe, accessible and secure environment, buildings and facilities that shall comply with government standards, and licensed and competent security personnel; b) a mechanism for students to help in crime prevention, safety and security of the concerned HEI and TVI.

Enumerates the duties and responsibilities of the Safety and Security Committee which shall include: a) formulation of a Safety and Security Strategy; b) formulation of crime prevention programs; c) coordination with HEI/TVI officials in the maintenance of peace and order; d) recommendation to the HEI/TVI the conduct of seminars or training on crime and drug prevention and control; e) intensive information drive on the Safety and Security Strategy; and f) submission to the CHED or to the TESDA the composition of the SSC and its Safety and Security Strategy, as well as its program of activities and projects.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HIGHER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION since 2020-01-20

rows.author: J089
rows.title_full: AN ACT INCORPORATING THE VALUE OF RESPONSIBLE, FAIR, AND TRUTHFUL USAGE AND ENJOYMENT OF SOCIAL MEDIA IN SCHOOLS AND UNIVERSITIES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Aims to cope with the mercurial rise of the influence and prevalence of the use of social media by the youth 
and/or students in their unavoidable daily immersion to these phenomena.

Proposes to include social media awareness in the curricula of primary and secondary education in public and private schools, for the purpose of inculcating among the youth and/or students how various types of social media:  helps in the effective and efficient dissemination of information, and in shaping public discourse and opinion; helps in fostering a more participative democracy, and in upholding truth and the veracity of facts, figures, and events; and responsible and fair use and virtues of discernment and critical-thinking in its use and/or enjoyment.

Seeks to include social media awareness as part of the NSTP, particularly in the Literacy Training Service (LTS) and the Civic Welfare Training Service (CWTS); and as part of private sector´s Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR)

rows.author: F402
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE DEPARTMENT OF DISASTER RESILIENCE, DEFINING ITS MANDATE, POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.title_short: Creating The Department Of Disaster Resilience, Defining Its Mandate, Powers And Functions
rows.abstract:
Creates a Department which shall be the primary government agency responsible for leading, organizing, and managing the national effort to reduce disaster risk, prepare for and respond to disasters, recover and rehabilitate, and build forward better after the occurrence of disasters. 

Provides the Department the authority to orchestrate different actors, policies and programs for disaster risk reduction and management; and to receive, administer, mobilize, report, monitor and oversee the utilization of the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund, recovery and rehabilitations funds, and donations for disaster risk reduction and management. 

Establishes the National Disaster Operations Center (NDOC) which is a center equipped with the necessary tools and systems to monitor, manage, and respond to disasters in the country; the Alternative Command and Control Center (ACCCs) which are command centers established in other locations to provide supplemental support to the NDOC; and the Disaster Resilience Research and Training Institute (DRRTI) which shall be a platform for providing training and for collecting, consolidating, managing, analysing, and sharing knowledge and information to improve or enhance disaster resilience.

Authorizes joint operational supervision with the following: a.) (DOST) over the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA), the Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHILVOCS); b.) (DENR) over the Geo-Hazard Assessment and Engineering Geology Section of the Mines and Geosciences Bureau (MGB); c.) (DOH) over the Health Emergency Management Bureau (HEMB), and d.) DILG over the Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP).
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2020-09-22, transmitted to the Senate on 2020-09-24 and received by the Senate on 2020-09-24
